name: cli
algorithm: Build one argument vector of n arguments (n/10 groups of --verbose, --count=<c>, --name n<c>, --level <3c>, --tag=t<c>, then the positionals f<j> up to n), then parse it reps times with each language's standard argument parser; per rep add count + level + len(name) + len(tag) + the positionals' count + verbose + len(files[rep mod len(files)]) (README.md).

skip.c: no std argument parser: ISO C has none, and getopt_long (POSIX, GNU) is not in the MSVC CRT this target links
skip.rust: no std argument parser: Rust std has std::env::args only (clap is not std); no crate stands in
skip.zig: no std argument parser: Zig std has the process argument iterator only
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the parser has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum checks that both parsers read the same values
notes: Idiomatic standard library (plan/06-m6.md 4.1): Mk gen cli.Args(Opts)'s emitted Opts.Parse, whose strs and positionals are views of the vector (no allocation: the positionals are one contiguous run); Go flag.FlagSet with five flags defined once (the analogue of Mk's compile-time generation) and Parse per rep. Arguments per second = n x reps / median. Checksums from the Go column and a hand count of the pseudo-code (std-cli session 2); verify through tools/bench before timing.
